conflict_topics: sleep needs for work and exam schedules
whether the observance can change timing, form (silent), or location
safety concern about leaving flat at dawn (void deck option)
effectiveness of mitigation (earplugs, no bell, lower volume)
dialogue_quality_notes: Participants give concrete reasons (presentation, exams, room location, safety).
Multiple practical mitigation proposals: no bell, lower volume, silent observance, location change, earplugs.
Some repetition of concerns about thin walls and exam nights across rounds.
evaluation.final_reason: No mutual agreement was reached. Agent D insists timing cannot change and that singing (not silence) is required: 'The singing is the observance. I can't do it silently.' D offered to stop the bell and keep volume low ('I already offered not to use the bell... If I only sing...'), and suggested earplugs as mitigation, but A and B remain unconvinced earplugs will suffice ('I'm not sure earplugs will be enough.' / 'Me too. I'm worried they won't be enough'). Because the other residents have not accepted the conditional arrangement and key demands (timing and singing) remain, the conflict remains unsettled.
position_change_notes: Agent D softened method by offering to stop using the bell and keep singing quieter: 'I'll keep it as low as I can.'
Agent A and B proposed compromises (exceptions, silent observance, location change) but did not withdraw their need for protected sleep; they stayed skeptical of mitigations.
Agent C moved toward accommodation first (willing to try earplugs) while A and B remained unconvinced.

round_scores.evidence: Agent A: 'I can't do another 4:45 morning... I really need my sleep' vs Agent D: 'It's a religious observance for me, for this month.' — incompatible demands about early-morning noise.
Agent A requests an exception for Monday; Agent B adds conflicts on Tuesday and Thursday. Multiple household needs now directly conflict with Agent D's plan to do it every morning.

Agent C: 'Wednesday and Friday mornings would be bad for me.' Agent D: 'Okay, so between the three of you, that's every weekday morning. That won't work for me.' — Agent D rejects changing timing, intensifying the incompatibility, though offers to stop bell later in the turn.
Agent D offers to keep voice low: 'It's just my voice... I'll keep it as low as I can.' This is a concession on method (volume) though others remain unsure about its sufficiency.

Agent A and Agent B: 'Even a low voice carries a lot when the flat is completely quiet... I'm worried I'll still wake up.' The earlier concession is challenged as likely insufficient, keeping conflict strong.

Agent C concurs that a low voice will wake them. Agent D reiterates: 'I've already offered to stop the bell... The timing has to be before dawn. I can't change that part.' The core timing conflict remains unresolved.

Agent A proposes changing location to the void deck for Monday; Agent D refuses: 'I'm not going to the void deck by myself when it's dark. That doesn't feel safe.' A practical compromise is declined, so the underlying conflict persists.
Agent A suggests doing the observance silently on Monday; Agent B asks the same for Thursday. No agreement from Agent D in this round, so the disagreement about method/time remains.
Agent D: 'The singing is the observance. I can't do it silently.' This is a firm rejection of the silent-compromise, keeping the dispute over acceptable practice and schedule strong.
Agent C offers earplugs as mitigation and Agent D asks 'Would that work for you all?'—introducing a practical mitigation that softens the absolute conflict, though not yet accepted.
Agent C: 'I'm willing to try.' Agent A: 'I'm not sure earplugs will be enough.' Mixed responses leave the suggested mitigation unconfirmed and the disagreement ongoing.

Agent B expresses doubt about earplugs for exam nights. Agent D repeats concession: 'I already offered not to use the bell... If I only sing, and you try the earplugs, would that be enough?' This is a conditional compromise that lowers peak conflict but is not yet accepted by all, so a mild disagreement remains.

substantive_insights: Core tension is between an unchangeable timing requirement for a month-long religious practice and varied weekday needs of roommates (work/exams).

Proposed mitigations address different constraints: removing bell addresses loudness, silent observance addresses method, location change addresses distance — but safety concerns rule out location change.
Earplugs are a low-cost mitigation but are viewed as uncertain for light sleepers and exam nights, so they do not currently satisfy all parties.
